title: Finite transactional service and DAG timing do not complete an autonomous threshold
statement: A private fixed-support Poisson module has acquire-all, reversible clean-prefix abort, commit-forward after unknown input consumption, ownership-loss guards and durable epoch/consumed/output records. Clearing cannot erase a committed record. The reported 46656-state check tests one outstanding port, not global epoch wraparound. A finite clearing/service word with probability >=[gamma_min/(e Lambda)]^ell gives a conditional availability tail; the requested channel still requires a valid fresh request and ready input. Repairing a damaged ledger is not quantum-information repair. In deterministic physical-time bins, valid local Lindblad interpolation gives fault-set diamond norm <=(epsilon tau)^|F|; coherent V costs 2||V||. Bounded-neighborhood schedule/overflow events plus uniform contact-fault weights give eta_box<=C[exp(a)-1+r^(1/R)], a=J epsilon_g+2v tau. Conditional geometric service gives valid closed-DAG time O(depth+log outputs) without independent siblings. Restarting an entire depth-d transaction instead costs ((1+mu/gamma)^d-1)/mu in mean time. Shared stalls and locally liftable clock winding invalidate broader unearned claims. Encoded request/epoch/ownership/Pauli records, inner EC during outer waiting, causal noise confinement and an actual asynchronous-cut decoder remain missing. A same-resource active comparator can run the identical generator. Reset entropy, heat and work are extensive in space and time. No autonomous memory threshold, trusted raw flag, native basin or microscopic contact implementation is established.
